focus: What a parent hub is, in files
noveltyJustification: All six findings are new hub-structure evidence; the hub was previously known only as a precedent name from the topic.
ruledOut: Treating a parent hub as a large single skill
Making a tool packet the default

findings.label: A parent hub is two small registries: hub-router.json (version, routerPolicy with defaultMode, handoff and fallback, per-mode signals) and mode-registry.json (hub name plus per-mode workflowMode, packet, packetSkillName, packetKind, router, default).
The hub SKILL.md is a packet picker, not a capability: it picks the packet, hands stage two to that packet's ROUTER.md, and the packet's SKILL.md holds the contract.
Routing is two-stage and bounded: stage one picks the packet from registry and signals, stage two is the packet router, so a request reads only the routing of the packets it uses.
The default mode is the workflow packet and a strictly CLI-named request starts in the named tool packet, with CLI names matching whole words only.
A hub ships consistency checkers: check-route-table.py proves hub files, registry packets and routers agree and that no packet SKILL.md re-embeds a router, while route-replay.py scores packet chains.
Each hub packet is itself a full package with ROUTER.md, SKILL.md, graph-metadata, leaf manifests, changelog, benchmark and playbook, so hub conversion composes packages rather than flattening them.
